title: Music & Theatre
tagline: Ritual bells, the scholar's qin, court orchestras, Noh, kabuki, kunqu, pansori and Peking opera, to Takemitsu and Isang Yun
hero_file: 湖北博物館曾侯乙編鐘.jpg
hero_caption: The bronze bell set of Marquis Yi of Zeng, c. 433 BC, Hubei Provincial Museum
intro: The music and musical theatre of China, Japan and Korea, from the ritual bells of the Zhou and the solitary art of the qin to the court orchestras of the Tang, Heian and Joseon, the great stage traditions of Noh, kunqu, bunraku, kabuki, pansori and Peking opera, and the composers who met Western music after 1868. Much of this music is anonymous or was shaped by generations of performers, so many entries name a tradition or lineage rather than a single composer. Pictures are instruments, early scores, paintings and woodblock prints from Wikimedia Commons; works still in copyright are not illustrated.
